problem.title: Delivery Cost per Mile
problem.statement: A local delivery costs 4 dollars for 0 miles, 10 dollars for 2 miles, and 19 dollars for 5 miles. The points lie on one line. By how many dollars does the cost increase for each additional mile?
hints: Compare cost change with mile change between two points.
Slope has units of dollars per mile.

solutionSteps.title: Compare two points
solutionSteps.body: From 0 to 2 miles, cost rises from 4 to 10 dollars: 6 dollars over 2 miles.

solutionSteps.title: Form the rate
solutionSteps.body: The slope is 6 ÷ 2 = 3 dollars per mile. The later pair confirms (19 - 10) ÷ (5 - 2) = 3.

validationMethods: slope from first and second points: (10 - 4) / (2 - 0) = 3 dollars per mile
independent slope consistency and option audit: (19 - 10) / (5 - 2) = 3, matching only choice B

problem.title: Right and Down
problem.statement: Point P is 4 units to the right of the origin and 2 units below the x-axis. What are its coordinates?
hints: Right is positive x; below is negative y.

solutionSteps.title: Read vertically
solutionSteps.body: Two units below the x-axis gives y = -2, so P = (4, -2).

validationMethods: axis-direction translation gives x = 4 and y = -2
independent quadrant audit: the description places P in quadrant IV; only choice D has positive x, negative y, and the stated magnitudes

problem.title: Which Point Is on the Line?
problem.statement: Which point lies on the line y = 2x + 1?
hints: A point is on the graph when its y-coordinate makes the equation true.

solutionSteps.title: Test the coordinates
solutionSteps.body: For (3, 7), the right side is 2(3) + 1 = 7, matching y.

solutionSteps.title: Reject the others
solutionSteps.body: Each other listed y-value differs from 2x + 1, so those pairs are not solutions.

validationMethods: independent exhaustive option residuals y - (2x + 1) are -1, -1, -1, 0, and 1, so only choice D lies on the line

problem.title: Distance Rate from a Table
problem.statement: A cyclist's distance from a checkpoint is 4 kilometers after 1 hour and 14 kilometers after 3 hours. If the relationship is linear, what is its slope in kilometers per hour?
hints: Use vertical change divided by horizontal change.
Keep the units attached to each change.

solutionSteps.title: Find the changes
solutionSteps.body: Distance changes by 14 - 4 = 10 kilometers while time changes by 3 - 1 = 2 hours.

validationMethods: independent rate reconstruction: two hours at 5 kilometers per hour adds 10 kilometers, taking 4 to 14; options audited

problem.title: A Falling Line
problem.statement: A line passes through (-1, 5) and (3, -3). What is its slope?
hints: Compute change in y over the matching change in x.
Use the same point order in numerator and denominator.

solutionSteps.title: Match the changes
solutionSteps.body: Moving from (-1, 5) to (3, -3), x changes by 4 and y changes by -8.

validationMethods: independent line reconstruction: y = -2x + 3 passes through both points; only choice B matches its coefficient

problem.title: Extend the Linear Pattern
problem.statement: A linear relationship contains the points (2, 11) and (6, 21). What is the y-coordinate of the point on the same line with x-coordinate 10?
hints: Find the change in y per unit change in x.
From x = 6 to x = 10 is the same horizontal change as from x = 2 to x = 6.

solutionSteps.title: Extend by a matching run
solutionSteps.body: From x = 6 to x = 10 is a run of 4, so y rises by (5/2)(4) = 10. Thus y = 21 + 10 = 31.

validationMethods: equal-run argument: each 4-unit x increase adds 10 to y, so 21 + 10 = 31
independent equation derivation: slope 5/2 and intercept 6 give y = (5/2)x + 6; at x = 10, y = 31; choices audited
